question: When every present word has equal weight, an ordinary not-all-equal birth weighs the old words by their number of extensions. A parent that holds two loose distinctions and owes one payment to a newborn is not told by ordinary growth which of the two to pay. Take that as the free setting. Can a lawful structure of parity and not-all-equal knots, with two holders per distinction, then give a four-correlation score above 2 while each observer's complete record has the same distribution for either far setting?
inputs: The recorded structures, engines and panels named in the pre-registration; the seeds it fixes.
forbidden_inputs: Any definition changed after a value is seen; any outcome of this study before the freeze; for the learner, labels of test items, orientation, letter templates and the three-lit-pixel clue.
primary_observable: The tables named under 'Runs and stop rule' of the pre-registration.
comparators_or_controls: The gates and controls of the predictions table (row G) and the control arms named in the definitions.
resource_budget: Each run under ten minutes and 12 GB on one CPU process; no long-running job.
first_executable_signal: The gate row G of the predictions table.
decision_rule: Each prediction is judged by its 'Fails when' column; nothing is tuned after values are seen.
stop_rule: One script lists side tables; one combines pairs; one computes the reference. If a hidden pair exceeds 2, the full structure is written out as a list of knots, every word of the four finished structures is enumerated by brute force, the local-explanation test is run, and a policy keyed to an old value is tested on it. The study stops when the class is exhausted and the reference and targeted search are done.
nonclaims: An exploratory study on named populations and classes. A finite census proves no all-size statement. Every reading, weighting and start named under 'What is supplied' is a scaffold.
